structured_output.analysis: The budget is 403/128 = 3.1484 bits. iso_3.15 averages 3.14795 bits [E514ab09c524e], so I have roughly 2e5 bits of headroom. That is far less than one MLP cell costs to move up a bit width (about 3.1M weights per cell). Any swap of bit widths would have to be paid for by dropping a 3-bit cell to 2-bit. Every retrieved layer loses a lot at 2-bit: 27.up_proj rht_gptq_int2 is 0.0349 against gptq_int3 0.0057 [E829dc44cee68, Ef04d8aa7bded], and 1.up_proj rht_gptq_int2 is 0.0271 against rht_gptq_int3 0.0061 [E07ef99eb5de4, E0564bc6ad1eb]. A funded swap would therefore probably lose more than it gains. On the method choice, the high-loss layers already use their best method at the same bit width. For example, 27.up_proj gptq_int3 measures 0.00572 against rht_gptq_int3 0.00774 [Ef04d8aa7bded, E8972491007e7], and 3.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 measures 0.00642 against gptq_int3 0.00706 [E6f4f7ea296d5, Ec98ddfd45576]. The remaining levers that cost no bits are the GPTQ options. I chose activation-order quantization (act_order) and a damping change; both leave the stored bits unchanged. There is also a gap between the predicted single-layer sum of 0.398 and the measured 0.436 [E514ab09c524e], so these option changes need to be measured on the full recipe.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: No bit cost: turn on act_order=true for every GPTQ-family method and keep the iso_3.15 cells, which measure KL 0.436 at 3.148 bits [E514ab09c524e]. The loss is concentrated in 3-bit up_proj cells, such as 27.up_proj gptq_int3 at 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded], whose activation kurtosis is 1090 [E24beed188b6a]. Quantizing high-activation columns first should help those cells most.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp05
proposals.rationale: No bit cost: act_order=true plus a higher damp=0.05 on the iso_3.15 cells (KL 0.436 [E514ab09c524e]). Predictions sum to 0.398 but the measured KL is 0.436 [E514ab09c524e], which suggests calibration overfitting. Stronger damping could make the 2-bit cells hold up better on validation, for example 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065].

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_lowbit
proposals.rationale: No bit cost: act_order=true only on the 2-bit and 3-bit GPTQ methods, which hold the loss concentration. Examples are 3.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00642 [E6f4f7ea296d5] and 18.gate_proj rht_gptq_int2 [Eb1dd74cd6447]. The 4-bit cells are left at default so this run separates the effect from the first proposal; base KL 0.436 [E514ab09c524e].
